newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ZOFF SAYS HE'S ONLY A STOPGAP AT CRISIS-HIT LAZIO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZOFF SAYS HE'S ONLY A STOPGAP AT CRISIS-HIT LAZIO.

text.p: Dino Zoff, the replacement for fired coach Zdenek Zeman at Lazio, has promised that another man will take over next season.

"I had to accept, I am a Cirio employee," the Lazio president told the daily Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper, explaining why he was returning to the bench. Cirio is the company headed by Lazio owner Sergio Cragnotti.
Zeman, a Czech, was dismissed on Monday.

"Cragnotti asked me to help for the rest of the season and I agreed," Zoff said, adding that he would stay until June as coach and would remain president at the same time. "For next season we will seek other solutions."
Zoff is now officially Lazio's president, coach, board member and trainer of the club's goalkeepers.
"It is an atypical situation and we had to take emergency measures," said the 1982 World Cup-winning goalkeeper, whose 112 international caps are an Italian record.
On Sunday, Lazio lost 2-1 at home in the league to Bologna, their second successive home defeat.
That knocked them down to 12th place in serie A and in danger of relegation for the first time since 1988 despite having three of the top scorers from last season.

Zeman, a taciturn Bohemian who fled his homeland in 1968, has been criticised by former players, notably Croat Alen Boksic who left Lazio for Juventus at the end of last season, for his intensive training methods and tactical rigidity.
He had been due to leave at the end of this season.
The club also lost key Italian international midfielder Roberto Di Matteo to Chelsea over the summer and Dutch midfielder Aron Winter to Internazionale.
Relegation to serie B, as well as uncertainty over the coaching staff, would be a major blow for a club that has said it wants to be the first in Italy to get a bourse listing.
Cragnotti said last week he wanted Lazio to be quoted as soon as possible, hopefully by next season.
Zoff, 54, coached Lazio from 1990 to 1994 when Zeman took over. He was also Italy's Olympic coach for two years from 1986 and has been tipped as a future Italy supremo.
Zeman, whose coaching career had been spent entirely with provincial clubs before Lazio, was the fourth foreign coach to lose his job in serie A this season.
His departure left just three foreign coaches in serie A, with one of those -- Sampdoria's Swede Sven-Goran Eriksson -- due to leave for Blackburn at the end of the season.

However Italian newspapers have speculated that Eriksson, who coached Lazio's arch-rivals Roma for three years in the 1980s and took them to the runner's-up slot in the league in 1986, might be tempted back to the capital.
